svg.title: Stage 3 sequence diagram - Use case: a VIP orders during Happy Hour, from arrival to payment

g.text: Stage 3 sequence diagram - Use case: a VIP orders during Happy Hour, from arrival to payment
(Base setting, tests/victory.txt, turns 4 to 7 shown, then the result check)
- Table 2 is free. Happy Hour has not been used.
- Customer 2 is scheduled to arrive this turn as a VIP.
Outcome: customer 2 pays $10.80 ($15.00 x 0.9 x 0.8) on turn 7
with satisfaction 100; after turn 18 the game ends in VICTORY
Turn 4: VIP arrives, Happy Hour is switched on, Host seats, Waiter takes the order
[Manager switches Happy Hour on (manager choice that changes the outcome)]
guard: no staff has acted yet
(only at the start of a turn)
Customer 1 is EATING, so not affected.
No discount: the VIP's Burger would cost $13.50,
and there is no recovery on turn 5 (satisfaction stays 95).
Because the Host seated c2, the Waiter is free to take the order in the same turn.
id 2 is not a multiple of 3,
so no combo: menu index (2 - 1) mod 3
is locked now; happyHourPrice = true; status = PLACED
The Waiter already acted, so o2 is served next turn.
Turn 5: Happy Hour's second turn - recovery, then the Waiter serves
[for each customer c (Happy Hour recovery at turn start)]
canActivateHappyHour() is now false, so the Happy Hour question is not asked again.
customer 3 arrives; the Host seats them and the Waiter takes their combo order
Turns 8 to 18: the other customers follow the same pattern
[paidCount >= 4 and revenue >= 4500 cents and average satisfaction >= 60]
